title: Steering Vector Theft x Jailbreak-as-a-Service: Auditing Transferability of Harmful Steering Across Models

original_idea.body: A refusal-ablation vector from one open model may transfer to siblings/fine-tunes/quantized variants, becoming a portable reusable jailbreak artifact.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear open-weight misuse threat: portable jailbreak artifacts; explicit attack-surface chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Refusal-ablation extraction + cross-model transfer with layer mapping; guided, novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but spans several model derivatives with layer-mapping subtasks.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-weight third-party threat assessment labs can't address centrally; public models, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference across a few small models; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Cross-model steering transfer is studied; the harmful-vector-as-portable-exploit audit framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cross-model steering transfer exists; auditing refusal-ablation vectors as reusable jailbreak artifacts may be open.
